The type must be one your team declares in `emits`. Use message_agent for something aimed at one agent, escalate_to_supervisor for a decision. Rate-limited; refused when the cause chain is deep.
read_events              Recent events on the bus (tickets, assignments, gate runs, staging, agents). Use to look back over what happened.
check_setup              Whether the system can do what is asked: which machines fill the worker and reviewer roles (AI agents, programs), the kind of work (tasks or code), the gate's tests, the capacity limit, what Orchestra runs, how each collector's last round went, and what each installed plugin's check says against the configuration (a missing tool, a dirty worktree, a bad setting). Call it first when a ticket blocks or keeps being rejected, or a request is not met.
read_config              The project's orchestra.toml as it is, whether it can be changed now, and its recent commits; whether the owner has a private overlay, and each key it sets (secret values left out).
list_processes           The programs Orchestra's launcher keeps running (its runtime record: state, pid, restarts, last exit code, log) and the collectors orchestra.toml declares, with the last line of each one's log.
read_machine_log         The end of a machine's log: a program's or a collector's (by its name in orchestra.toml or the process list, e.g. shell_worker, tasks.scheduler), orchestra-host for Orchestra's own, or the log a machine announced.
list_metrics             The metrics catalogue: every series name in the project's own store, its labels, when it was last written and how many points in the last hour. A measurement that is not here is not being stored.
get_model                The system dynamics model Orchestra discovered from the metrics, for a diagnosis: the series each stock is, flows with their equations and the machines attributed to them, and the series the last discovery left out, with why. To experiment on the model, read_model.
read_instrument          A declared instrument ([[collect]], [[scrape]] or [[sources]]) as Orchestra sees it: when it last wrote, how many points, failures and its last error, the end of its log, and the latest values of each series it stored in the last minutes. Use it after set_collector to see that the measurement is being stored.
check_sources            Another time-series store ([[sources]], or a url before declaring one): where it is, whether its credentials are present (never their values), whether it answers and which API endpoints work.
source_schema            What a store has: without match, every metric name with its type (or a guess from its name), and its levels (gauges of amounts held, with what each holds); with match, those metrics in detail (series, labels, help, label values).
preview_query            What a PromQL query returns over a recent window: each series' labels, points, min, max, last and a sparkline. From a source, or with neither source nor url from the project's own store.
infer_source             What Orchestra infers to read from a store for discovery: its metric families (kind, stats, interval, labels and their roles), the definitions it keeps (query, view, kind, score) and those it leaves out with why.
read_transcript          An agent's transcript, trimmed to the turns you ask for: what it was told, what it called and what it said. By agent (its latest session) or by session id, around a time.
snapshot                 The task system's whole picture in one answer: tickets with why each waits, milestones, capacity, the pipeline, and which machine instance holds each assignment.
modeling_guide           How to read the system dynamics model and experiment on it: what stocks, flows, equations, eras, trust and verdicts mean, the equation language, and how to test a hypothesis before you believe it. Read it before your first experiment.
read_model               The system dynamics model Orchestra discovered from the metrics, summarised: each stock with its level now, each flow with its ends, its equation in the equation language, its origin and error, and whether to trust it.
read_series              Measured history of stocks (levels), flows (rates) or measured inputs, summarised: first and last, range, mean, trend an hour, the latest readings. points: true gives the points themselves, paged.
read_eras                The eras (each announced change to the system begins one) and what changed at the last boundary: each flow's numbers before and after, with how sure that it changed.
read_observability       Which stocks what is measured determines, which are hidden, and the model's modes (how fast it settles).
check_equation           Whether an equation parses in the equation language against the model (or an experiment's draft), and what it reads.
read_predictions         Predictions and their verdicts (passed, no effect, side effect, model wrong elsewhere, interrupted, undecided), with the numbers each was judged by.
list_experiments         Experiments, newest last: id, title, status, owner, runs, prediction.
read_experiment          One experiment: what its draft changed from the base model, its runs, its prediction.
diff_experiment          What an experiment's draft changed from its base model: flows, stocks, the scenario.
read_run                 An earlier run of an experiment again, summarised, or whole with raw.
declare_stock            Declare a stock the owner expects to accumulate, measured or not yet ("I'm going to create a Features stock"). Then find how to measure it (propose_measurements) and start recording (add_instrument) in the same turn.
declare_effect           Declare an effect: a measurable consequence of the system nobody owns (latency, error budget, review backlog age, on-call load). Kept like a declared stock.
set_target               A target on a stock or effect (a level) or a flow (a rate), judged on its mean over a window: met, missed or unknown ("land five a day" is a flow target).
propose_measurements     Record the ways to measure a declared stock or effect, in order, after you looked: the store (list_metrics, read_series), the repository's own reports (a CI JUnit report through orchestra.instruments.test_reports; never run a suite in the working tree), other plugins' counters, another store or company system (named and costed only: never previewed until the owner clears it), and a simulated placeholder last. It only records. Whether one needs the owner's approval is decided from what it reads, not from what you say.
add_instrument           Start recording one option at once: a script of at most 100 lines you write (to the state directory, instruments/<name>.sh), or the command or URL the option proposed; tried first exactly as Orchestra runs it, then its [[collect]] or [[scrape]] entry goes in the owner's private overlay, one act. Refused over 100 lines, with what looks like a secret, for an option that needs approval or reaches another host, or when the trial fails (with its output); nothing is written then. It records as a draft that expires in 24 h unless the owner keeps it (keep_instrument). where: repo tries it, then hands it to the Coordinator for .orchestra/instruments/<name>.sh.
keep_instrument          Keep a draft instrument the owner chose: quote their words, or call it after their expect click on its series. It stops expiring, its draft flag comes off (discovery reads it from then) and the option is chosen.
mark_expected            Mark a discovered stock or flow expected ("yes, track that one"): always drawn, with the pin; a ghost when a version leaves it out.
ignore                   Ignore a discovered suggestion: it moves to the collapsed "ignored" group; nothing is hidden.
link                     The owner says a declared stock is a discovered one ("yes, that's Features"): a manual binding, origin declared, an assumption until fitted. It never renames the discovered stock. A confirmed machine's expected edits that waited for it are published then.
declare_machine          Declare a machine by name ("Create a new Universal Machine called Feature Count Improver"): its envelope and its kind's fields (invariants, steps, uses for a Universal one; command and the rest for a Programmatic one), every guess named in guesses. It stays unconfirmed and never runs until the owner confirms. Read the map first (read_design, read_events, read_model); use existing event types where one has the purpose. A Universal one is drafted under drafts/<name>/; say its cost.
refine_machine           Change a declared machine while the owner talks ("watch DONE and REJECTED tickets", "make it 12am every day"): give only what changes; each change is recorded with the value it replaced, all or none. With the owner's words quoted it applies at once on an unconfirmed machine; otherwise, or on a confirmed one, it is a proposed change the owner confirms. The Universal | Programmatic switch is switch_kind.
switch_kind              The Universal | Programmatic switch, on the owner's click (request) or their words (quote): the kind changes and the spec is kept (to Programmatic, the Universal description is the program's specification). On a confirmed machine switched to Programmatic, its agent stops and the program goes to the Coordinator.
declare_event            Declare an event type's purpose (a new type in an existing family, when no observed one has the purpose). Never one nothing would publish.
declare_expected_effect  A machine's expected effect, as a draft prediction: what it should change, rates where you can, judged after a horizon of at least three of its runs. Published as your prediction only when the owner confirms the machine.
confirm                  The owner confirmed ("confirm it", quoted, or their click: request). A stock, effect or a pending change is declared; a Universal Machine is declared and set running: its spec, role and agent records written to the state directory's machines/, its expected effect published.
discard                  The owner discarded it (quoted, or their click: request): kept only in the history; a draft, and a discarded stock's instruments, leave no file.
read_design              The declared layer in one read: every declared and proposed element with its state, link and guessed fields; each machine's fields; each event type's declared publishers and listeners and who was heard publishing it or announced listening; the open items (unconfirmed proposals, pending changes, unanswered requests, unpublishable drafts); the last changes; the draft instruments; and the refinement pass's latest proposal.
